description: Data Science graduates and students from UABC Ensenada, Mexico
summary: ANALOG(IA) is an open, reproducible pipeline and web platform that finds the places on Earth that most resemble specific sites on Mars. We profiled six Martian sites (Jezero, Gale, Eberswalde, Holden, Saheki and the Olympus Mons caldera) from NASA HiRISE, CTX and THEMIS data plus ESA HRSC terrain models, and built a global catalog of 708,793 arid, uninhabited 5 km patches of Earth from Copernicus DEM, ESA WorldCover, GHS-POP and NASA MODIS. Each Earth patch is ranked against each Mars site with a weighted Gower distance over relief variability, slope, roughness and albedo, and the best candidates are grouped into distinct field regions with HDBSCAN. The method recovers known analogs (Atacama, Death Valley and Wadi Rum rank in the top 1%) and proposes new ones, such as the Mojave Desert for Jezero (95.3% similarity) and the Pamir for Olympus Mons. Results can be explored on an interactive 3D Mars globe with an AI assistant that explains each match. ANALOG(IA) turns analog selection from expert intuition into a systematic, scalable and auditable search that mission planners and field-test teams can reuse for any new landing or base site.
details: WHAT IT DOES Given any Martian site, ANALOG(IA) returns a ranked, clustered list of the Earth locations whose terrain most closely matches it, and explains why each one matches. We applied it to six sites of high exploration value: landing sites (Jezero, Gale), ancient deltas and fans (Eberswalde, Holden, Saheki) and a volcanic caldera (Olympus Mons). HOW IT WORKS 1. Mars profiles: we downloaded DTMs from the NASA Planetary Data System (HiRISE, CTX and ESA HRSC) and THEMIS brightness-temperature (IRPBT4) and albedo (VISALB4) scenes through the PDS Orbital Data Explorer. Each site was resampled to about 125 m/pixel and summarised as elevation standard deviation, median and 95th-percentile slope, median and 95th-percentile roughness, albedo and brightness temperature. 2. Earth catalog: we tiled the land surface of six continents in 0.5 degree patches and processed the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM at 463 m/pixel (the MOLA scale). Urban, cropland, forest, populated and water-dominated cells were removed with ESA WorldCover 2021 and GHS-POP 2023, and each remaining patch was split into ~5 km subpatches with MODIS albedo (MCD43C3) and land surface temperature (MYD11C3). Result: 708,793 clean, arid, uninhabited subpatches with 71 variables. 3. Similarity search: for each Mars site we computed a weighted Gower distance to every Earth subpatch (30% relief variability, 30% slope, 30% roughness, 10% albedo), using one shared normalisation so scores are comparable across sites. Temperature was only used in exploratory scenarios, because Martian and terrestrial temperatures are not physically equivalent. 4. Geographic clustering: the 500 closest subpatches per site were clustered with HDBSCAN on haversine distance, giving 15 to 21 distinct field regions per site (silhouette 0.60 to 0.71). Each cluster has a geographic, a geomorphological and an "optimal analog" representative point. 5. Platform: a Three.js web app renders Mars from MOLA elevation and Viking MDIM imagery, plus a high-resolution HiRISE patch for Jezero. Users pick a Martian site, see its Earth analogs with their variables, and can ask an AI assistant to explain the match using only the computed values. RESULTS Best analogs: Jezero - Mojave Desert, USA (95.3% similarity); Olympus Mons caldera - Pamir (94.5%); Eberswalde - Tibetan Plateau (92.1%); Saheki - Tarim/Kunlun margin (81.2%); Holden - Mauritania (78.3%); Gale - Aksai Chin (71.6%). Known Mars analogs (Atacama, Death Valley, Wadi Rum) rank in the top 1% of the global ranking, which supports the method. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Analog sites are used to test rovers, instruments, EVA procedures and habitats before missions, but today they are chosen mostly by expert knowledge and logistics. ANALOG(IA) adds a quantitative, global and reproducible ranking that surfaces less-studied candidates and documents exactly why a place qualifies. Any new Mars or Moon site with a DTM can be added with the same code, and all code and data are open (MIT and CC BY 4.0). LIMITATIONS Mars sites are profiled at ~125 m/pixel and Earth at 463 m/pixel, so matches describe broad landforms rather than fine surface texture. Composition and mineralogy are not modelled. Future work: tune clustering and weights with a multi-objective NSGA-II search, harmonise resolutions, and add lunar Artemis sites with LOLA DEMs. TOOLS Python (rasterio, GDAL, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, joblib, earthaccess, pyhdf, hdbscan, scikit-learn), Jupyter, R, JavaScript/Three.js, Netlify Functions and the Google Gemini API. Website: https://analogia2026.netlify.app/
